newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Securum says sells 10.2 pct in Akzo Nobel.
newsitem.headline: Securum says sells 10.2 pct in Akzo Nobel.

text.p: Swedish Securum said on Friday it sold another 10.2 percent stake, or 7.26 million shares, in chemicals group Akzo Nobel for 279.20 guilders a share.
The price corresponded to the share's closing price on the Amsterdam bourse on March 6, the company said.
The shares were sold to a number of foreign financial institutional investors and the divestment will free up capital of 7.9 billion crowns, Securum said.

After the transaction, Securum holds three percent in Akzo Nobel but this stake will also be divested as it is connected to options with a price of 215 guilders a share. The options will expire on May 1, 1998, the company said.

Securum is a state-owned company set up to manage assets pledged by Swedish banking group Nordbanken during the bank crisis in the early 1990s. Securum aims to divest all assets at a reasonable price.
